name: sol_mccc_10
description: Ethereum-specific opcode/address-derivation assumptions break zkSync Era compatibility
question: The source file in `source` contains code that relies on Ethereum-mainnet-specific EVM behavior—such as computing CREATE2 addresses with the standard formula keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode)), using extcodesize/extcodehash to distinguish EOAs from contracts, depending on SELFDESTRUCT semantics, or assuming exact opcode gas costs—without any zkSync Era-specific adjustment or fallback, causing incorrect address prediction, EOA detection, gas accounting, or destruction behavior when deployed on zkSync Era, excluding contracts explicitly documented as Ethereum-mainnet-only deployments.
criteria: A function inline computes a CREATE2 deployment address using keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode)) and uses that address for critical logic without any zkSync-specific branch
Code checks extcodesize(account) == 0 or account.code.length == 0 to determine whether an address is an EOA before allowing/blocking an action
Code calls selfdestruct(...) expecting immediate contract removal and ETH transfer as the sole cleanup/refund mechanism
Code uses raw PUSH0 opcodes or hardcodes Ethereum mainnet gas cost constants (e.g., fixed gas stipends for calls) that are assumed identical across chains
